In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a system of perfectly competitive firms is efficient in the sense that the allocation of commodities to the firms is Pareto optimal, and in the sense that there is no Pareto optimal allocation in which the set marketed commodities is larger than that marketed by the perfectly competitive firms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Profit Criterion, in the presence of perfect competition, leads to an efficient allocation of economic resources.
we have shown that the standard competitive model may be completed by a model that determines the set of markets endogenously.
the organization of economic activities is a matter of efficiency, and that it is not possible to have efficiency without the Profit Criterion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Profit Criterion is not sufficient for the existence of an efficient set of commodities.
a perfectly competitive firm is a small firm in a limiting economy.
the Profit Criterion is not the criterion that is used in the organization of economic life, but rather the criterion that results from the organization of economic activities.
